title: Reading the Cosmological Constant from Dwarf-Galaxy Rotation Curves: The a0-Line, Its Systematic Floor, and the de Sitter-Modified-Inertia Inversion
description: Gas-rich dwarf-galaxy rotation curves invert, through a single fixed dimensionless constant, to a value of the cosmological constant that agrees with the Planck measurement to within a factor of ~2 -- a striking coincidence, given that the galactic-side determination uses NO cosmological input whatsoever -- but the measured low-acceleration scale a0-hat = (0.84-1.36)e-10 m/s^2 is a systematics-limited box that straddles both footings on which the framework's horizon term can be defined, and the ~21% distinction between them cannot be decided on current data. That is the central result, and each clause is load-bearing. In a de Sitter-Unruh modified-inertia (MI) framework the low-acceleration scale is tied to the cosmological horizon by a0 = cH_Lambda/Z with Z = sqrt(32pi/3) = 5.78881, giving a0(canonical) = c^2 sqrt(Lambda/32pi) = 9.355e-11 on the pure-Lambda (dark-energy-density) footing, or a0(ALT) = cH0/Z = 1.1305e-10 on a total-density (cH0) footing -- two footings 20.9% apart, carried on every dimensional number. CREDIT UP FRONT: the interpolation kernel nu = sqrt(1+1/y) is Milgrom's (Phys. Lett. A 253:273, 1999); squaring the framework law g_obs = sqrt(g_bar^2 + a0 g_bar) yields the exact identity E = g_obs^2 - g_bar^2 = a0 g_bar (the missing-gravity excess is a straight line through the origin, slope a0, at every acceleration); the identity follows from squaring Milgrom's kernel, and the distinctive content is (a) the exact constancy epsilon = E/(a0 g_bar) = 1 at all g_bar -- a fingerprint whose CONSTANCY rival kernels violate -- (b) the cH_Lambda/Z coefficient, and (c) the Lambda-inversion. Fitting the slope on the gas-dominated SPARC subsample (Lelli, McGaugh & Schombert 2016), where the absolute stellar mass-to-light (Upsilon) swing is cut ~71% (7.90 to 2.29e-11), gives the box above. Two dominant systematics are mapped with independent, committed, exit-0 verification: TRGB-class distances collapse the estimator-choice systematic but distance is NOT the binding wall (and reveal the banked low median was a Hubble-flow-distance artifact), and an external-Upsilon lever tightens a0 by 2-12% through partial self-calibration (a0-Upsilon posterior correlation rho ~ -0.7 to -0.8, never -> -1) yet leaves the footings undecided even in the perfect-M/L limit (~1.94 sigma) -- the true floor is gas-mass calibration, whose coherent contribution hypot(sU_coh, sysG) = 1.037e-11 exceeds the footing-split threshold |Delta|/2 = 9.75e-12 at any galaxy count. Inverting through Lambda = 3 Z^2 a0-hat^2/c^4 recovers Planck's Lambda to a factor ~2 (full-gas GLS central 1.59x, +1.45 sigma; median/independent-machinery central 1.08x, +0.24 sigma, the better-supported and closer estimate). IMPORTANT NON-INDEPENDENCE: the factor-2-in-Lambda is the factor-~1.4-in-a0 squared -- the same single comparison, 'does the rotation-measured a0 equal cH_Lambda/Z', re-expressed, not independent confirmation across many decades, and NOT a test of the postulated normalization Z, which appears on both sides. A log-flat Occam comparison favours the zero-parameter horizon prediction by +0.60 bans (canonical) / +1.04 bans (ALT) -- substantial, not decisive, prior-fragile. The cleaner the distances, the more the central OVERSHOOTS Planck (TRGB-tightened 2.03x, +2.76 sigma), so the sharpest data mildly DISFAVOUR the canonical footing rather than confirm it; a separately identified g_bar-correlated systematic (residual M/L / response-noise, a mild tension with the framework's own epsilon = 1 fingerprint) makes that overshoot's interpretation uncertain. The value of a0 and the sign s = -1 remain postulates throughout; what is tied to the horizon is the SCALE. Not a theory of everything -- the a0 reframing and its measurement only. Every load-bearing claim is backed by a committed, adversarially verified, exit-0 script.
notes: Referee-graded writeup (draft -> 4-reviewer adversarial panel [physics/honesty/citation/rigor] -> revise). The panel corrected a physics mislabel: the observed decline of per-point a0 = E/g_bar with g_bar is NOT kernel/nu-shape (the framework's epsilon = E/(a0 g_bar) = 1 exactly, sympy-verified, leaves no shape to leak, and the decline is opposite-sign to what rival kernels predict) but an unmodeled g_bar-correlated systematic and a mild tension with the framework's own epsilon = 1 fingerprint. Companion to 'The Zimmerman Theory of Gravity' (the forward Lambda -> a0 statement) and 'MI Field Theory Results 2026' (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21403470). Both a0 footings carried on every dimensional number. Milgrom 1999 credited as the identical nu-kernel; the identity is a re-expression of his law. No 'proves / solved / definitive detection' language. https://github.com/carlzimmerman/zimmerman-formula
